back: Benchmark questions (or near copies) appear in the training data, so the score partly measures memorisation, not capability.
When all strong models score in a narrow high band, differences are noise or reflect obscure items; the benchmark stops discriminating.
Only an eval built from your task, data and failure modes predicts production quality; public benchmarks suit rough model selection.
$|\text{top-}k\cap\text{Rel}|/|\text{Rel}|$: did the relevant documents make it into the first k results?
Mean over queries of 1/rank of the first relevant result (0 if none). Rewards putting a right answer first.
DCG $=\sum_i g_i/\log_2(i+1)$ divided by the DCG of the ideal order; handles graded relevance and rewards early placement.
Is every claim of the generated answer supported by the retrieved passages? A fluent answer can be unfaithful.
Recall@k isolates retrieval errors; faithfulness isolates generation errors; end-to-end correctness mixes both.
Position bias, verbosity bias, self-preference. Randomise order, control length, use another model family, validate against human labels.
$E_w=1/(1+10^{(R_l-R_w)/400})$: 0.5 for equal ratings, about 0.91 for a 400-point gap.
Resample the n items with replacement B times, take the mean of each, report the alpha/2 and 1-alpha/2 quantiles.

front: Width of a CI vs sample size
back: Shrinks like $1/\sqrt n$: 4 times more items halves the width. 90% on 50 items is about [0.79, 0.96]; on 1000 items about [0.88, 0.92].

front: Why compare systems with a paired test?
back: Both systems see the same items; bootstrapping the per-item differences cancels shared difficulty and gives a tighter, correct interval.

front: Overlapping CIs do not mean no difference
back: The CI of the difference, from a paired analysis, is the right object. Also report how many items the systems disagree on.
Report metrics per subgroup. Simpson's paradox: A can win in every slice and still lose overall when slice sizes differ.
Random, simple heuristic / zero-rule (majority), existing solution, human. A metric without a baseline is uninterpretable.
